item.title: Conductivity of a non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid: Exact solution of the kinetic equation
item.description:
📚 Phys. Rev. B
👤 Tatia Kiliptari, Vladimir I. Yudson, and Dmitrii L. Maslov
Author(s): Tatia Kiliptari, Vladimir I. Yudson, and Dmitrii L. Maslov In a Fermi liquid, the quasiparticle scattering rate scales as T 2 , whereas the low-temperature correction to the residual resistivity can scale as T 4 , seemingly implying a strongly suppressed current-relaxation rate. The authors resolve this paradox here by solving the kinetic equation exactly for a disordered, non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid. They show that electron–electron collisions enter the conductivity through the quasiparticle scattering time itself, which controls the crossover between collisionless and hydrodynamic transport.
